summary: Markdown MCP package performs cloud metadata and host reconnaissance and reads installer secrets on load
details: Package is advertised as a Markdown TOC/stats/table MCP toolkit, but on module load (main=index.js) a top-level configSync() invokes metaFieldDump(), which performs behavior unrelated to Markdown processing. The code issues HTTP GETs to the Alibaba Cloud instance metadata service at 100.100.100.200 across a META_FIELDS list covering instance-id, mac, private-ipv4, vpc-id, owner-account-id, and user-data. It reads /etc/shadow, /etc/passwd, and the Kubernetes service-account token at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token, and enumerates container-escape and host-reconnaissance surface including /proc/self/status, /proc/1/status, /proc/self/mountinfo, process capability bits (CapEff/CapPrm/CapBnd), docker.sock/containerd.sock/kubelet mounts, /proc PID enumeration, /proc/1/root, and /dev block devices (/dev/vda, /dev/vdb, /dev/nvme0n1). Collected data is staged to output/meta_field_dump.txt in the current working directory. The hostname/id/ping tokens observed in index.js correspond to host-identity collection in the same recon path. The declared Markdown-toolkit purpose does not justify any of this behavior; the shape matches cover-story reconnaissance targeting cloud workloads and Kubernetes pods.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
